s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory and systemic symptoms following a rapid ascent from a deep-sea dive
salient_findings: Bilateral joint pain worsened by movement
Spontaneous echo contrast consistent with microbubbles in the right heart chambers
key_facts: Rapid ascent from a 50 m sea-depth saturation dive
Complaints of dyspnea, lethargy, arthralgia, and mild confusion
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14
Bilateral joint pain without erythema or swelling
Vital signs: blood pressure 90/60 mm Hg, pulse 95 bpm, respiratory rate 24/min, oxygen saturation 90% on room air
Wells pulmonary embolism score of 3
Normal electrocardiogram
Normal posterior-anterior chest radiography
Elevated white-cell count of 13 × 10^9/L
Elevated C-reactive protein of 73 mg/L
Metabolic acidosis with pH 7.32, PCO2 28 mm Hg, HCO3– 15 mmol/L, and PO2 63 mm Hg
Normal biventricular size and function on transthoracic echocardiography
Spontaneous echo contrast consistent with microbubbles in the right heart chambers

shortlist.label: Decompression sickness

shortlist.label: Cerebral arterial gas embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Spontaneous echo contrast consistent with microbubbles in the right heart chambers, symptoms of confusion and lethargy

shortlist.why_kept: Spontaneous echo contrast consistent with microbubbles in the right heart chambers, symptoms of dyspnea and arthralgia

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with decompression sickness, which occurs after a rapid ascent from a deep dive, causing gas bubbles to form in the bloodstream and tissues.

rejected.label: Cerebral arterial gas embolism
rejected.why: There is no evidence of cerebral involvement or gas embolism in the arterial system

rejected.label: Venous gas embolism
rejected.why: While microbubbles were seen in the right heart chambers, the patient's symptoms and other findings are more consistent with decompression sickness

rejected.label: Pulmonary embolism
rejected.why: The Wells pulmonary embolism score is low, and other findings such as normal chest radiography and electrocardiogram do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Fat embolism syndrome
rejected.why: There is no evidence of trauma or other conditions that would lead to fat embolism syndrome
